items.title: Microsoft 365 AiTM Phishing Bypass: BigBear PhaaS Analysis
items.excerpt: This analysis details how the BigBear Phishing-as-a-Service operation leverages Adversary-in-the-Middle proxies to bypass Microsoft 365 multi-factor authentication. Defenders will find actionable indicators of compromise, proxy infrastructure mappings, and mitigation strategies for enterprise identity environments.

items.title: Tracking BigBear 2.0 Evilginx2 Phishing Campaign | CloudSEK
items.excerpt: CloudSEK researchers track the evolution of the BigBear 2.0 campaign, highlighting its use of Evilginx2 to harvest session cookies and bypass MFA controls. The report provides network-level detection rules, domain reputation data, and defensive recommendations for securing cloud identity gateways.

items.title: The Device Code Phishing Tsunami: What We’re Seeing in the Wild
items.excerpt: LevelBlue documents the rapid proliferation of device code phishing attacks that exploit Microsoft’s device authorization flow to bypass traditional MFA. The article outlines real-world attack patterns, infrastructure indicators, and defensive strategies for monitoring and restricting device code sign-in events.

items.title: Advanced Phishing-as-a-Service: BigBear 2.0's Sophisticated Evasion of Microsoft 365 MFA Across Hundreds of Enterprises
items.excerpt: Eximus breaks down the operational scale of BigBear 2.0, demonstrating how its PhaaS model enables threat actors to systematically evade MFA across hundreds of organizations. Infrastructure defenders gain insights into campaign infrastructure, credential harvesting techniques, and recommended identity hardening controls.

items.title: Bypassing the Gatekeepers: How a Global Phishing Campaign Turns Google's Infrastructure into a Trust Proxy
items.excerpt: This report examines a sophisticated campaign that abuses Google’s legitimate infrastructure to establish trust proxies, effectively bypassing perimeter security controls. IT defenders learn how to identify proxy abuse patterns, monitor for anomalous OAuth flows, and implement stricter conditional access policies.

items.title: Inside an AI‑enabled device code phishing campaign
items.excerpt: Microsoft Security researchers analyze an AI-driven campaign that automates device code phishing at scale. The post details how machine learning optimizes victim targeting and payload delivery, while providing defenders with telemetry-based detection methods and conditional access policy recommendations.

items.title: Inside Knight Office, a New M365 AiTM Phishing Kit | Huntress
items.excerpt: Huntress provides a technical deep dive into Knight Office, an emerging AiTM phishing kit targeting Microsoft 365 tenants. The analysis covers kit architecture, session hijacking mechanics, and detection signatures. Defenders receive guidance on blocking malicious proxy domains and reinforcing identity verification workflows.

items.title: Russian hacker group Laundry Bear exploits Zimbra zero-click flaw to target Western government, critical infrastructure
items.excerpt: This briefing covers Laundry Bear’s exploitation of a zero-click vulnerability in Zimbra collaboration servers to compromise government and critical infrastructure networks. Defenders receive patch guidance, network detection signatures, and incident response steps for mitigating unauthenticated remote code execution risks.
